reuse.why: The new daily-skip rule is added inside the existing applyWeekendRule, and every pre-existing caller (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, the schedule template) keeps going through it.

duplication.why: It collapses the two copied weekend ternaries in schedule-template into one adjustOccurrence closure, but adds two separate lookahead heuristics (WEEKEND_SKIP_LOOKAHEAD in getNextDate and an inline count * 7 in getUpcomingDates).

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to the weekend logic, and parseRecurDate in rule-utils only passes frequency through to the schedule data.

scope.why: Every edit is needed for the skip rule (rule, data plumbing, callers that now handle null, and tests).

maintainability.why: The design is clean overall, but the nullable return value spreads null handling to every caller, and the template loop condition `(nextDate ?? nextBaseDate) < nextMonth` is hard to read.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All weekend handling goes through applyWeekendRule.

disguised_duplication.where: The lookahead appears twice with different constants (shared/schedules.ts WEEKEND_SKIP_LOOKAHEAD and server/schedules/app.ts count * 7). Both are visible, not disguised.

one_place.where: applyWeekendRule in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts decides skip versus move for daily schedules, and all three code paths call it.
